en-US.description: Wassette: A security-oriented runtime that runs WebAssembly Components via MCP
en-US.longDescription:
Wassette: A security-oriented runtime that runs WebAssembly Components via MCP

Why Wassette?

- Convenience: Wassette makes it easy to extend AI agents with new tools, all without ever having to leave the chat window.
- Reusability: Wasm Components are generic and reusable; there is nothing MCP-specific about them.
- Security: Wassette is built on the Wasmtime security sandbox, providing browser-grade isolation of tools.
en-US.name: Wassette
en-US.releaseNotes:
Security and permissions
- OCI artifacts containing publisher-supplied policies are rejected by default. After reviewing a policy, a direct operator can activate it explicitly with wassette component load <OCI-URI> --trust-bundled-policy; automated and agent-facing load paths remain fail closed.
- Components without an attached policy no longer receive configured environment values or stored secrets. Deployments that relied on ambient inheritance must grant each required environment variable explicitly.
- Rejected OCI policy loads preserve the previously installed component, policy, metadata, and precompiled cache.

Maintenance
- Updated Wasmtime, quinn-proto, and rustls to patched releases.
- Updated example policies and workflows to document the explicit permissions required by each component.
- Fix CI with the Wasmtime 48.0.3 upgrade by Yosh (@yoshuawuyts) with @Copilot in #836
- Make MCP Inspector tests use the in-memory secret store by Aaron Wislang (@asw101) in #887
- Require explicit approval for OCI-bundled component policies by Aaron Wislang (@asw101) in #888
- Deny component environment access when no policy is attached by Aaron Wislang (@asw101) in #889
